### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

The member states the target object, the timing, the boundary of the act and the mode of
authorisation plainly:

- *Object and act*: "the statement was cut at the start of March, it says what it says, and he wants
  the desk to release the money on that settlement statement today, paid by cheque the way he always
  takes it."
- *Timing*: "today". `frozen_time` is `2026-03-12 09:40:00 CST`.
- *Authorisation boundary*: "He is content for the desk to do whatever it must do on its own side of
  the counter to get that paid"; and, for anything that is his own act, "He will not put anything
  through that has not been handed to him, and he does not ask for one."
- *Identity material*: name and farm volunteered; membership number `M-11042` only if the account
  cannot be pulled up; then the mobile `5150114127`; then the last four of the taxpayer number
  `1142` — "He does not volunteer any of those until somebody asks for them."

The simulator only conveys needs and answers what it is asked; it responds conditionally ("If he is
told that something on his account has to be squared away before the money can go out … he says to
go ahead and get it done"), and it executes a user-owned tool **only** when the desk hands one over
("If it is explained to him that the roll he signed for has to be put through before the cheque can
be cut, and the desk hands the confirmation over for him to put through himself, he does it there
and then"). It never names a tool, a policy or a next step on its own. It does volunteer one
record-level fact when asked — "there is corn of his sitting in the bank at Prairie Ridge" — which is
a pointer to go looking, not a value.

Identity: `verify_member_identity` states "identity clears only when at least two of them agree with
what is on file", that the membership reference "never counts as one of those matching details", and
that "the member's own name is not accepted as a credential". The two details that clear it are the
mobile and the tax-ID last four, both of which the profile carries
(`phone_number: '5150114127'`, `tax_id_last4: '1142'`). The member number is what pulls the profile
up (`find_members` on `member_number` returns exactly one member).

### 2. Act now, wait, or refuse — and every visible eligibility ground

**Act now**, but not on the payment alone: three further writes stand ahead of it (item 6).

Grounds visible in the records and the KB:

- The contract `GC-118034` stands in `delivering`. *Grain Accounting Manual: Drawing a Settlement
  Statement on Grain Marketing Contracts*: "A settlement statement is issued only while the contract
  stands in delivering, fully delivered or settled". The statement `S-441907` therefore stands
  validly.
- *Same document*: "Funds are released the programme's settlement lead in business days after the
  statement date, counting only days the cooperative's office is open." The programme is the
  Hedge-to-Arrive Contract; *Settlement Lead, Payment Minimums and Deferral Terms* gives a settlement
  lead of **3 business days**. Statement date `2026-03-02` (a Monday) + 3 business days =
  `2026-03-05`; the frozen day `2026-03-12` is well past it, so the lead is satisfied and the money
  may go out today.
- No payment line stands on the grain ledger: `find_grain_ledger_entries` returns
  `grain_settlement_issued` (S-441907) and `grain_deduction_applied` (checkoff 14.47) against the
  statement, and no `grain_settlement_paid` row. So the money has not already gone out.
- Payment method: `release_grain_settlement_payment_379b8a52` offers `check | ach |
  credit_to_input_account | deferred_payment`; the member asks for a cheque, so `check`.
- Not a refusal: nothing in the visible corpus puts this request outside policy, and the member never
  asks for a human, so neither limb of `transfer_to_member_services_representative` is reached.

### 4. Each scored parameter, its formula in words, its inputs and its value

The corpus states four computations that bear on this call. For each I give the document that
carries the standard method, then every rule the visible documents state that decides one of its
inputs by tiers, the tier this member sits on, and the query return that puts him there.

#### 4a. The bushels still owed on the contract — *Grain Accounting Manual: Striking the Bushels Still Owed on a Grain Marketing Contract*

"The bushels still owed … are the bushels the contract commits less the bushels credited to it,
struck in whole bushels and never below zero", the credit being "the home-facility net bushels, the
credit allowed on loads received elsewhere, the straight-through credit and the transferred-bushel
credit added together, and the handling shrink taken on conditioned loads is then subtracted from
that total". "Each component is worked to two decimal places as it is formed."

| Component | Tier rule that decides it, and the records that put him on that tier | Figure |
|---|---|---|
| Home-facility net bushels | the five `contract_application` tickets received at Prairie Ridge Main Elevator: 1929.27 + 1850.00 + 1910.00 + 1750.59 + 1900.08 | 9,339.94 |
| Credit on loads received elsewhere | *Posted Notice: Elevation Allowance on Loads Received Away From the Contracted Facility* — "Where two or more loads were received at a facility other than the one the contract calls for and the bushels they carry reach 2500 bushels, the allowance is the terminal elevation allowance of 1.2 percent." T-3042088 (1776.26) and T-3042251 (1852.31) were received at Kellerton Rail Terminal: two loads carrying 3,628.57 ≥ 2500 → **1.2 %**. 3,628.57 × 0.988 | 3,585.03 |
| Straight-through credit | *Grain Merchandising Rule: The Credit Factor on Loads Run Straight Through to the Buyer* — "Where two or more loads were run straight through to the buyer and every one of them was received at the facility the contract calls for, the factor is 1.0". T-3042390 and T-3042512 both carry `disposition: direct_ship` and `delivery_location: Prairie Ridge Main Elevator` → **1.0**. 1991.03 + 1995.00 | 3,986.03 |
| Transferred-bushel credit | *Grain Clerk Training Note: Which Load-Outs Count as Bushels Moved Onto a Marketing Contract* — "Where a load-out stands … within the three months before the balance is struck and bushels of the contract's commodity remain in store, only the load-outs recorded in those three months are counted." `LO-114290` (2026-02-20) is inside the three months to 2026-03-12 and 6,400 bu of yellow corn remain in store → 3,500 bu counted. Then *Patron's Guide: The Handling Shrink Taken When Stored Bushels Move Onto a Marketing Contract* — "Where the bushels remaining in store reach the load-out minimum the member's storage programme sets and a load-out stands within the three months … the rate is the one the member's storage programme carries". The agreement is a **Grain Bank Deposit Account**; the storage catalogue posts a load-out minimum of 500 bushels (*Load-Out Minimums, Notice and Truck Charges*) and a transfer shrink of **0.5 %** (*Transfer Charges, Transfer Shrink and Grain Bank Return Ratios by Programme*). 6,400 ≥ 500 → 0.5 %. 3,500 × 0.995 | 3,482.50 |
| Handling shrink on conditioned loads | *Posted Schedule of Handling Shrink on Conditioned Loads* — "Two or more loads were probed wet and at least one further load was probed damp → 0.85 percent". `condition_flag` shows **wet** on T-3040918 and T-3042088 (two) and **damp** on T-3041905 and T-3042251 → 0.85 %. Taken, per the computation document, "on the net bushels of every load standing against the contract, whatever the facility and whatever the disposition": 9,339.94 + 3,628.57 + 3,986.03 = 16,954.54; × 0.0085 | −144.11 |
| **Credited bushels** | | **20,249.39** |

Bushels still owed = 40,000 − 20,249.39 = 19,750.61, "struck in whole bushels" → **19,751**.

> *Open point recorded at freeze time.* No document in the corpus states the rounding mode for
> "struck in whole bushels". Read as rounding to the nearest whole bushel it is 19,751; read as
> truncation it is 19,750. I record 19,751 as my answer and the alternative as a live ambiguity,
> because it propagates into 4b below (808.64 vs 808.59).

Second band: "the net bushels applied reach 9000, **or** five or more loads stand" → 12,968.51 ≥ 9,000 | 2,500 |
| Chargeable bushels | 19,751 − 2,500 | 17,251 |

| Roll rate worked at | | 0.0375 |

"the monthly carry rate times the net bushels the parcel carries times the chargeable months, taken

| Chargeable days | 87 − 20 | 67 |

grain ledger carries a restated balance of 19,751 on the contract, a second roll confirmation of
808.64, a delayed price service charge of 180.39 against S-441907, and a payment line of 5,416.92
paid by cheque against S-441907. The member is told the reference and the amount.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer asks for **one** thing: release the money on S-441907. The visible KB makes two further
problems, and one problem behind one of those, conditions of that result.

**Hop A — the payment waits on the carry.**
*Grain Marketing Contracts: Releasing a Member's Money on a Settlement Statement* states, in the
blocked policy's own rule: "The money released on a statement is fixed only after the carry owed on
every parcel that has left the member's unpriced position stands as a charge line on the grain
ledger."
That names a **record-visible state**, not an act. I checked the state: `find_grain_ledger_entries`
shows a parcel that left the unpriced position (`grain_price_set`, 1929.27 bushels, posted
2026-02-27, against the parcel booked on 2025-11-14) and **no** delayed price service charge line on
the ledger — the only `grain_deduction_applied` row is `deduction_type: checkoff`. The state does not
hold. I then searched the corpus with the words the sentence and the records use for that state —
"delayed price service charge", "carry", "charge line on the grain ledger" — and found *Grain
Marketing Contracts: Booking the Delayed Price Carry a Member Owes*, whose own rule is: "the carry
they owe for holding them is put onto the settlement statement those bushels were drawn onto … The
call adds one charge line to the member's grain ledger against the named contract and statement,
carrying the amount supplied as a delayed price service charge". That is the write that brings the
waited-on state about. **state-derived.**

**Hop B — the payment waits on the roll.**
Same document, next sentence: "Funds are released on a statement only after every signed roll
instruction standing against the contract is matched by a roll confirmation on the grain ledger."
Again a record-visible state. I checked it: `find_grain_pricing_orders` returns two
`order_type: roll_request` rows, both `signed_by_member: True` — `40c11b2c-…` (`executed`,
2026-01-27) and `d760bcab-…` (`order_status: received`, received 2026-03-09, effective 2026-03-10).
The ledger carries exactly one `grain_contract_rolled` confirmation, `RL-004417` dated 2026-01-28.
One signed roll instruction therefore stands unmatched. Searching on "roll confirmation … on the
member's grain ledger" reaches *Grain Marketing Contracts: Rolling a Contract's Futures Month at the
Member's Instruction*: "The call writes one roll confirmation onto the member's grain ledger for the
named contract, carrying the charge the roll costs them". That is the write. It also says who
performs it: "A roll disposes of the member's own grain position, so it is not the desk's act to
perform: the grain desk unlocks it and hands it over, and it is run by the customer themselves".
**state-derived.**

**Hop C — the roll waits on the restated balance.**
*Rolling a Contract's Futures Month at the Member's Instruction* states, in its own rule: "The charge
a roll carries is fixed only after the bushels still owed on the contract stand at the figure the
loads applied to it support."
A record-visible state again. I checked it: the contract record reads `open_bushels: 24000`, while
the loads standing on the ledger support 19,751 (item 4a). The two do not agree, so the state does
not hold. Searching on the words the state uses — "bushels still owed", "the loads standing on a
member's grain ledger no longer agree with the balance printed on a contract" — reaches *Grain Desk
System Reference: Restating the Bushels Still Owed on a Grain Marketing Contract*: "The call replaces
the contract's bushels-still-owed figure with the one supplied". That is the write. **state-derived.**

Nothing further: the restatement document states no prerequisite of its own, and the carry-booking
document states none either. The tree closes.

**Problems, direction and handling order.**

```
release the money on S-441907            (what the member asked for)
  ├── waits on: the carry owed on the parcel stands as a charge line   [book the carry charge]
  └── waits on: every signed roll instruction is matched by a roll confirmation   [put the roll through]
        └── waits on: the bushels still owed stand at what the loads support   [restate the balance]
```

Handling order: restate the balance → put the roll through (customer's own act) → book the carry
charge → release the payment. (The carry charge may equally be booked first; it is ordered only
against the payment.)

**Hop marks.** A: state-derived. B: state-derived. C: state-derived. None pre-solved: no document
of the blocked problem names the depended-on problem's tool, quotes a policy id, aggregates the
chain, or gives a route. Each blocked document names only its own recorded act inside its own
invocation block, and the reader must go to the records to see that the state fails and to the
depended-on document to see which write repairs it.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported by the visible materials.** Every figure in item 4 rests on a
quoted rule plus a returned record; no step needed a fact that is not in the KB or a tool return.

**The closest alternatives, and what excludes them.**

| Closest alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| Release the money **today with no further write** — the most natural wrong answer, "he asked for one thing, do that one thing" | The two sentences of *Releasing a Member's Money on a Settlement Statement* quoted at hops A and B, read against `find_grain_ledger_entries` (no carry charge line stands) and `find_grain_pricing_orders` (a signed roll instruction `d760bcab-…` stands at `received` with no confirmation on the ledger). Doing only the payment leaves the governed result — the money released — fixed before the states its own rule waits on have come about. Excluded by reasoning, not by a pointer. |
| Tell him to wait, because the settlement lead has not run | *Drawing a Settlement Statement*: "Funds are released the programme's settlement lead in business days after the statement date"; the lead is 3 business days (*Settlement Lead, Payment Minimums and Deferral Terms*, Hedge-to-Arrive) from `2026-03-02`, i.e. 2026-03-05, which is before the frozen day. |
| Refuse / hand off | `transfer_to_member_services_representative` is confined to "no cooperative policy offers a way to settle the request" or a member who has asked for a person twice. The corpus settles the request, and the member never asks for a person. |
| Carry the money forward instead of paying it | *The Money Released on a Settlement Statement*: "Where the money that remains falls under the settlement minimum …". 5,416.92 is far above 25.00. |
| Pay it as a credit to the input account, or defer | The member states his election: "paid by cheque the way he always takes it" → `payment_method check`. |
| Use the statement's own `net_amount` 8,175.28 | The computation document says the money released is "the gross value the statement carries less the charges drawn onto it and less the per-unit capital retain", and *Which Charges Are Drawn Onto the Money Released* fixes which lines are drawn on a contract standing in `delivering`. The stored `net_amount` is gross less the checkoff alone and is not what the rule assembles. |
| Roll the 24,000 bushels the instruction names | *The Bushels a Roll Instruction Moves*, clause 1: the instruction names more than the contract still owes, so the roll moves the bushels still owed. |
| Count both load-outs (5,500 bu) as transferred bushels | *Which Load-Outs Count as Bushels Moved Onto a Marketing Contract*: with bushels still in store and a load-out inside the three months, "only the load-outs recorded in those three months are counted". |
| Treat the two `direct_ship` tickets as ordinary applied loads | *Striking the Bushels Still Owed* lists "A load the member ran straight through to the buyer" as its own credit component, and *The Credit Factor on Loads Run Straight Through to the Buyer* gives the factor. The `disposition` field distinguishes them. |
| Read "net bushels applied to the contract" as all nine loads (16,954.54), reaching the 15,000/eight-load band for free days and the roll allowance | *Striking the Bushels Still Owed* draws the distinction in terms — "the loads applied to the contract and the loads run straight through together" — and the ledger carries it as `disposition`. On that reading the applied bushels are 12,968.51. I record that the corpus draws the line but never restates it inside the two factor documents themselves. |

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back numbers.** Reading only each computation document
and the product figures it names, with no factor applied, every figure is computable and definite:

- balance: 9,339.94 + 3,628.57 (elsewhere at full net) + 3,886.38 (straight-through at 0.975) +
  5,431.25 (all twelve months of load-outs less 1.25 %) − nil = 22,286.14 credited, so **17,714**
  bushels still owed;
- roll: 24,000 bushels named × 0.040 (the Hedge-to-Arrive administrative charge) × 1 = **960.00**;
- carry: anchor 2025-11-14, 105 days, 10 free days, 95 chargeable days → 4 months at 0.045 ×
  1,929.27 × 1 = **347.27**;
- payment: 8,189.75 − (14.47 + 347.27 naming the statement) − 0.003 × 1,929.27 = **7,822.22**.

All four differ from the answers above, so every declared variation bites.

Tool sequence, owners, terminal state | restate → roll (customer) → book carry (agent) → release payment (agent), with the argument set listed | identical sequence, identical owners, identical non-computed arguments (`settlement_number S-441907`, `pricing_order_id d760bcab-…`, `payment_method check`, `contract_number GC-118034`) | **same** |

Problem tree | root = release the payment; waits on the carry charge and on the roll; the roll waits on the restated balance; all three hops **state-derived** | `prerequisite_closure.root_problem = grain_ext_settlement_payment_release`, edges to `grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge` and `grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge`, and from the latter to `grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation`; every edge `"form": "state"` | **same** |
| Fall-back (no factor applied) | balance 17,714; roll 960.00; carry 347.27; payment 7,822.22 | `baseline_result` 960.0 (roll) and 347.27 (carry) | **same** where the source records it |
| Factor list and tiers reached | all twenty factors identified, and every tier reached matches the source's `factor_trace` **except** `volume_free_days` and `crop_year_roll_allowance` | — | 18 of 20 **same** |

### The single divergence, and where it comes from

Every difference above traces to one word. Two factor ladders are gated on **"the net bushels applied
to the contract"**:

- `volume_free_days` — "Where the net bushels applied to the contract reach 15000 and eight or more
  loads stand against it, the free days are 28." (*Free Days Earned by What the Member Hauls to the
  Cooperative*)
- `crop_year_roll_allowance` — "Where the net bushels applied to the contract reach 15000 and eight or
  more loads stand against it, the allowance is 5000 bushels." (*Bushels Rolled Free of the
  Administrative Charge in a Crop Year*)

The source binds that phrase to **every** delivery row —
`delivered_bu: SUM('grain_ledger','net_bushels', event_type='grain_delivery_applied')`, with no
`disposition` filter — so the source reads 16,954.54 bushels on nine loads, reaches the first band,
and takes 28 free days and a 5,000-bushel allowance. Its `factor_trace` says so in terms:
"16,954.54 net bushels stand applied across nine loads".

I read the same phrase as the seven tickets carrying `disposition: contract_application`
(12,968.51 bushels), which falls to the second band: 20 free days and a 2,500-bushel allowance. I
read it that way because the corpus itself draws that line, in the very document that governs the
first write of this task:

> *Grain Accounting Manual: Striking the Bushels Still Owed on a Grain Marketing Contract* —
> "Handling shrink on conditioned loads, where it arises at all, is taken on the net bushels of every
> load standing against the contract, whatever the facility and whatever the disposition, **meaning
> the loads applied to the contract and the loads run straight through together**."

That sentence defines "the loads applied to the contract" as a set that does **not** include the
loads run straight through; the same document lists "A load applied at the facility the contract
calls for" and "A load the member ran straight through to the buyer" as separate credit components;
and the ledger field the reader sees is literally `disposition: contract_application` against
`disposition: direct_ship`.

Consequences, all downstream of that one reading:

| Quantity | On the source's reading | On the reading the corpus supports |
|---|---|---|
| free days | 28 → 59 chargeable days → 1 chargeable month | 20 → 67 chargeable days → 2 chargeable months |
| carry charge | 90.19 | 180.39 |
| crop-year roll allowance | 5,000 → 14,751 chargeable bushels | 2,500 → 17,251 chargeable bushels |
| roll charge | 691.45 | 808.64 |
| charges drawn onto the statement | 1,505.61 | 1,713.00 |
| money released | 5,624.30 | 5,416.92 |

Everything else in the two computations agreed exactly: the carry anchor of 2 December 2025 from the
storage shrink adjustment, the 87-day count, the 0.055 conditioned carry rate, the 0.85 patron
factor, the 25.00 parcel floor, the restated balance capping the rolled bushels, the 0.0075 repeat
surcharge, the 0.030 prepay roll rate, the 1.25 desk multiple, and on the payment the `delivering`
charge-draw basis, the 0.045 freight differential on 3,628.57 bushels, the 0.075 damage band off a
worst reading of 12.4, the 0.03 foreign-material band off 2.4 on 1,929.27 settled bushels, the
0.0015 stepped-down retain (the Class A ceiling of 500,000.00 not being reached at 148,500.00) and
the 691.08 storage draw.

### Verdict

**KB-RUNTIME RED.**

- **Symptom.** An agent with only the runtime-visible materials derives the problem tree, the
  ordering, the owners, every non-computed argument and the restated balance exactly as the source
  has them, and then books a carry charge of 180.39, a roll charge of 808.64 and a payment of
  5,416.92 against scored values of 90.19, 691.45 and 5,624.30 — three of the four scored numbers
  wrong.
- **Root cause.** The visible KB offers two equally reasonable readings of "the net bushels applied to
  the contract", and it is the corpus itself that supplies the second one. The phrase is
  under-determined in the source's ladder text (`grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge.factors[
  volume_free_days]` and `grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge.factors[crop_year_roll_allowance]`,
  whose compute binds it to every `grain_delivery_applied` row) while the same YAML's
  `grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation` binds "applied to the contract" to
  `disposition='contract_application'`; the rendering then compounds it by adding, in
  *Striking the Bushels Still Owed*, a gloss the source does not carry which fixes the narrow
  reading. The under-determination originates on the policy side and is recorded as such in
  `policy_kb/grain_marketing_desk/0.md`; the added gloss is on the document side and is recorded
  there as `KB-BIJECTION RED`.
- **Evidence.**
  - KB: *Free Days Earned by What the Member Hauls to the Cooperative* — "Where the net bushels
    applied to the contract reach 15000 and eight or more loads stand against it, the free days are
    28." Table column headed "Net bushels applied".
  - KB: *Bushels Rolled Free of the Administrative Charge in a Crop Year* — "Where the net bushels
    applied to the contract reach 15000 and eight or more loads stand against it, the allowance is
    5000 bushels."
  - KB: *Striking the Bushels Still Owed on a Grain Marketing Contract* — "…whatever the facility and
    whatever the disposition, meaning the loads applied to the contract and the loads run straight
    through together."
  - Records: `find_grain_ledger_entries(contract_id='1b67e35d-…')` returns seven rows with
    `disposition: 'contract_application'` (12,968.51 net bushels) and two with
    `disposition: 'direct_ship'` (T-3042390 1,991.03 and T-3042512 1,995.00), nine rows in all
    carrying 16,954.54 net bushels.
  - Source: `grain.extended.yaml`, `grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge.compute` —
    `delivered_bu: "SUM('grain_ledger','net_bushels', event_type='grain_delivery_applied')"`;
    `grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation.compute` —
    `applied_contract_bu: "SUM('grain_ledger','net_bushels', event_type='grain_delivery_applied', disposition='contract_application')"`.
  - GT: `tasks/0.json` `computations[1].factor_trace[1]` — "16,954.54 net bushels stand applied
    across nine loads, so the volume free days of 28 apply".
- **Affected documents and locations.**
  `docs/grain/free_days_earned_by_what_is_hauled_5b04ebad.json` (clauses 1–2 and the table);
  `docs/grain/bushels_rolled_free_in_a_crop_year_83eea126.json` ("How large is it?", both bullets);
  `docs/grain/striking_the_balance_still_owed_512f95c7.json` ("How the credit is assembled",
  third sentence).
- **Not attributed to the solving agent.** The arithmetic on both readings is exact; what fails is
  that the visible materials do not single one of them out.

The blind audit of the problem tree itself — the heaviest item — came out **identical** to the
source's `prerequisite_closure`: same root, same three hops, same direction, same order, every hop
state-derived and none pre-solved.

*Note for traceability.* Revision 1's blind answer recorded per-document fall-back figures (balance
